key_findings.finding: Standard thoracic mechanics divide ribs 2–6 primarily into pump-handle motion: the anterior rib/sternal ends move superiorly and anteriorly during inhalation and inferiorly/posteriorly during exhalation, chiefly about a transverse (mediolateral) axis through the costovertebral/costotransverse region. Ribs 7–8 are predominantly bucket-handle ribs: their lateral shafts move superolaterally on inhalation and inferomedially on exhalation, chiefly about an anteroposterior axis.

source_tools.relevance: PubMed search returned osteopathic rib-motion/dysfunction literature, although the database results do not directly state the axis terminology.

key_findings.finding: If a unilateral rib has reduced inhalation excursion but exhalation is normal or symmetric, the restriction is in inhalation; in standard osteopathic terminology this is an exhalation rib dysfunction (the rib is relatively depressed and cannot elevate), not an inhalation dysfunction. For ribs 2–6, the restricted motion is pump-handle elevation about the transverse axis; for ribs 7–8, it is bucket-handle elevation about the anteroposterior axis.

source_tools.relevance: Search results include an osteopathic case report explicitly describing a rib restricted from exhalation as an inhalation dysfunction, supporting the inverse naming convention used here.
